Refuse to modify a user with a higher role (#1132)

* Refuse to modify a user with a higher role

An owner could edit, demote or delete a site admin in their tree, since
the user endpoints only checked the caller's permissions, not the
target's role. In a single-tree setup, the first user is a site admin
and shares the tree with any owners. By changing the admin's e-mail
address and triggering a password reset, an owner could take over the
admin account.

Editing another user, changing their password and deleting them now
answer 403 if the user has a higher role than the caller. Users with
the same role can still act on each other, so co-owners can manage
each other.

* Look up both roles by user ID and refuse unknown users

The role check looked up the caller's name by ID and then their role by
name, and let the request through if either user could not be found. A
caller renaming themselves concurrently could make the second lookup
